$comment: Observation of what the client sends in the actor-connection window, captured by an instrumented everfall-netd. This is the differential that isolates why the client never leaves WaitingForActorGameConnection with our server while it leaves it in 167 ms against the Python lab.

context.lab_success: start actor game connection 10:00:13.210 -> actor game connection succeeds 10:00:13.377, with NO server message in between, so the rung is crossed by Carrier machinery and not by a ladder record
context.ours: start actor game connection -> WaitingForActorGameConnection -> State(...) is timeout, never crossing

client_records_seen_in_the_window.note: SM_CONNECT_REQUEST -> ANSWERED with the acceptance flight
a second connect request in the SAME datagram -> ignored ('only the first connect request of a datagram')
the client's chunked channel-0 record -> answered with SM_CT_ACKS
second channel-0 record -> answered with SM_CT_ACKS
SM_CT_ACKS, the client's own carrier acknowledgements -> IGNORED, repeating every ~113 ms

finding: SM_CT_ACKS is system id 6 (services/world/src/azoth_world/javelin/frame.py:29). Our server ignores the client's acknowledgements while the Python reference DECODES them (rep.py:4814, 'Decode the client's SM_CT_ACKS (Carrier.cpp WriteAckData format)') and maintains a window over them. So our server never knows which of its reliable datagrams the client acknowledged.
hypothesis_to_test: Processing the client's SM_CT_ACKS, as the reference does, is what lets the Carrier connection machinery complete on the server side so the client's actor game connection succeeds. The live run discriminates; it is not proven.
